text: Working nights at a petrol station, you learn to spot the weird ones.
This one stood outside the automatic doors. They wouldn't open for him.
So he knocked on the glass and asked if he could come in.
You said yes. Obviously. It's a shop.
He bought a bag of rice. Paid in coins from seventeen ninety.
And on the CCTV screen, you were serving nobody.
He leaned over the counter and said, you look tired.
You wake up on the floor at three thirty-three. The till's full. Nothing's missing.
Except the rice is everywhere. And you're counting it.
You decide you dozed off. You finish the shift.
By five, coffee smells like burning hair.
And you can hear the heartbeat of the man at pump four.
At ten to six, the sky goes grey. The back of your hand starts to smoke.
Your shift ends at six. Sunrise is six twelve.
And on his receipt, he's left a phone number.
